title: Putin Proposes Summit Next Month With Trump, Xi To End Ukraine War: Report
standfirst: The Kremlin has suggested holding the trilateral dialogue on the sidelines of the upcoming Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit, the report said.
lede: Russian President Vladimir Putin has proposed a summit next month with US President Donald Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping to negotiate an end to the four-year-old Ukraine conflict that would favour Moscow, the Wall Street Journal reported on Sunday, citing people familiar with the discussions. The proposed summit comes amid warming ties between Trump and Putin especially after the US President announced a deal to buy Russian diesel and signed an order on Friday waiving key sanctions on Moscow.

title: Loud Phone Calls, Music On Trains May Land You In Jail
standfirst: With mobile internet use growing, playing music, videos and other content through phone speakers on trains and at stations has emerged as an area of focus for authorities.
lede: Watching videos or playing your favourite songs on a train journey could soon come with a price - if the volume disturbs fellow passengers. Southern Railway has issued fresh instructions to curb loud music played through mobile phone speakers on trains and at railway stations, with fines of up to Rs 1,000 for violations. Those who repeatedly cause a nuisance despite warnings could face up to six months in jail and a fine of Rs 5,000. The railway has urged passengers to use earphones and respect others' comfort.

title: The Boy Who Copied Code From A Book Now Teaches the World AI
standfirst: Andrew Ng taught himself to code at five. Now the Google Brain founder and Coursera co-founder is coming to New Delhi for the NDTV World Summit 2026.
lede: Long before AI chatbots became an everyday staple, a little boy in Hong Kong sat typing lines of code from a book into a small computer. He wasn't trying to change the world, at least back then. He just wanted to play a video game. That boy was Andrew Ng. Decades later, he is one of the people who taught the world how machines learn. This week, he comes to New Delhi to speak at the NDTV World Summit 2026 on "AI at Scale: Building the Intelligence Economy."

title: Netanyahu's Reliance On India Ties Amid Thinning US Support For Israel
standfirst: This is not the first time Netanyahu has evoked India and his relationship with Prime Minister Narendra Modi to argue against Israel's growing isolation in the world and to demonstrate his...
lede: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu believed Israel is likely to face a hostile US administration in the future, potentially threatening its military assistance and strategic relationship with Washington. Speaking at an event days before Israel's October 27 election, the Israeli PM said the country must develop new international alliances, including with India and Latin American countries, to strengthen his country's position. Netanyahu's remarks came hours before he received a strong endorsement from US President Donald Trump, who publicly expressed his support for the Israeli PM's re-election bid just days before the country goes to the polls.

title: Speeding Thar Rams Scooter On Hyderabad Highway, Kills 2 Siblings
standfirst: Their scooter had reportedly stopped behind a DCM vehicle amid traffic congestion when a red Mahindra Thar allegedly hit it from behind.
lede: Dussehra festivities turned tragic for a family after a speeding Mahindra Thar rammed a scooter near Hayathnagar bus stop on National Highway 65, the Hyderabad-Vijayawada highway, on Sunday afternoon, killing a brother and sister on the spot and leaving a young girl seriously injured. Those who died have been identified as Edulla Naveen, 25, and his sister Baindla Rekha, 34, residents of Peddamberpet in Ranga Reddy district. Rekha's three-year-old daughter, Charvika, who was travelling with them, sustained serious injuries and was rushed to a hospital for treatment.

title: Ashtami And Navami: Halwa, Puri, Chole, And A Generous Helping Of Nostalgia
standfirst: For a young girl, Kanjak Puja is almost like a second birthday - a day to dress up, visit neighbourhood homes, enjoy halwa, puri and chole, and be treated like a little princess, just as many of us...
lede: In Hindu culture, little girls are considered little goddesses, representatives of the Devi, powerful, supreme, and kind. It is to honour the Devi that we observe Navratri, and what better way to culminate the nine-day festival than to treat little girls as nothing short of goddesses? They are welcomed into homes with love, their feet are washed, and they are served prasad as families seek their blessings. This is Kanjak, or Kanya Pujan, observed on Ashtami or Navami. For a young girl, Kanjak puja is quite a grand occasion, much like her birthday. Today, she is a princess, and she is going to make the most of this special day, just as many of us once did.

title: APPSC Group 2 Notification 2026 Out For 686 Posts: Check Registration Dates
standfirst: The APPSC Group 2 notification has been released for 686 posts. The link to register for the exam will be activated on November 10, 2026 and the last date to submit the form is November 30, 2026.
lede: APPSC Group 2 Notification 2026: The Andhra Pradesh Public Service Commission (APPSC) has released the Group 2 recruitment notification 2026 under Advertisement No. 37/2026. The drive aims to recruit candidates for 686 executive and non-executive vacancies across Andhra Pradesh. According to the official notification, the registration process will begin from November 10, 2026 and the last date to submit the form is November 30, 2026. Before applying for the exam candidates must go through the eligibility criteria. Along with the registration dates the notification also consists of vacancy details, exam pattern, syllabus etc.

title: Sucrose vs Glucose vs Fructose: What Is The Difference?
standfirst: Sucrose, glucose, and fructose are three varieties of sugar that have the same calorie content when measured by weight.
lede: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has proposed to prohibit the addition of sucrose and fructose to foods for infants up to six months of age. This proposed restriction aims to control early exposure to added sugars, which is linked to childhood obesity and related health problems. You must have come across the terms sucrose, glucose and fructose. While they are all sugars, your body absorbs them differently. title: Winter Yet To Set In, But Delhi's AQI More Than Doubles In 3 Days
standfirst: Delhi's Environment Minister Manjinder Singh Sirsa said on Saturday that Delhi has recorded 211 days of good, satisfactory and moderate air quality so far this year, its best performance since 2016,...
lede: A slight nip in the air signals the changing season, but winter is yet to arrive in Delhi. Yet, the national capital's air quality has deteriorated sharply over the past three days. Since Friday, Delhi's Air Quality Index (AQI) more than doubled as dry weather and slower winds allowed pollutants to accumulate. From 90 on Friday, the national capital's AQI rose to 159 on Saturday and 187 on Sunday, according to Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) data. Meanwhile, the temperature in Delhi and the national capital region (NCR) has fallen following the withdrawal of the monsoon. On Sunday, Delhi's temperature settled at 17.1 degrees Celsius, 1.3 degrees below the season's normal, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) said.

title: Security At Salman Khan's Home Increased After Attack On Tiger Shroff
standfirst: Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis enquired about Tiger Shroff's well-being on call. He has assured of strict action against those involved.
lede: The security outside actor Salman Khan's house in Mumbai has been increased after an assassination attempt was made on actor Tiger Shroff. Three shooters fired at Tiger Shroff's car while he was leaving a football stadium in Juhu, Mumbai. A member of the Lawrence Bishnoi gang took responsibility for the attack, citing his closeness to Salman Khan. Following the development, the Mumbai police have intensified the security at Salman Khan's Galaxy Apartments house and are checking every vehicle passing through the area as a precautionary measure.

title: Cine Workers Body Writes To Amit Shah For Tiger Shroff's 'Full Security'
standfirst: In the letter addressed to Home Minister Amit Shah, AICWA also listed several other demands after the firing incident.
lede: The All Indian Cine Workers Association (AICWA) President Suresh Shyamlal Gupta has written a letter to Union Home Minister Amit Shah over the firing on Tiger Shroff on Sunday (October 18) in Mumbai's Juhu area, demanding full security for the actor's family. Three rounds of firing were shot at Tiger's car, leaving his driver and an autodriver injured. The driver was reportedly struck by bullets, while the actor escaped without any gunshot injuries.

title: Tiger Shroff Was Tracked For 10 Days, Shooters Recced House, Gym: Sources
standfirst: The accused, one of whom is a minor, were in constant contact with their handlers through WhatsApp and Signal.
lede: Three men who carried out the attack on actor Tiger Shroff on Sunday evening in Mumbai's Juhu had allegedly conducted a recce of the actor's residence and gym prior to the shooting. The accused were allegedly tracking Tiger Shroff's movements and schedule for nearly 10 days, sources said. Three men riding a motorcycle opened fire at Tiger Shroff's car on Sunday evening when he was returning home from a football ground. Seven rounds were fired, targeting the vehicle's windshield and side windows. Five bullets struck the car, while two missed their mark.

lede: France has faced widespread protests and unrest amid public anger over rising costs and declining public services. Reports from October 17 described clashes and property damage in several cities, with incidents including fires and confrontations involving police. The demonstrations have put pressure on authorities as they work to maintain public order while responding to protesters’ grievances. While the situations differ from city to city, the developments have renewed debate over economic pressures, public services and the government’s response.
